title: Oncall: noisy SLO flares + missing metrics — investigation & tuning notes
body:
Summary:

This doc captures a real on-call investigation and a set of pragmatic tuning proposals after multiple short SLO burn alerts that turned out to be noisy and partially caused by missing/unstable metrics from the KV cache sharder. The goal is to record what we saw, initial mitigations we used, and longer-term changes to reduce pager noise without obscuring real regressions.

Incident timeline (high level):
- 2026-01-26 02:18 UTC: First SLO burn alert fired for hosted-api/response-latency P99 > 800ms for 5m (pager P1).
- 2026-01-26 02:21 UTC: Duplicate alert for hosted-api/throughput drop (SLO derived) and redispatcher-heartbeat-missing fired.
- 2026-01-26 02:25 UTC: Oncall routed to primary (Lena) and secondary (Ava). Initial triage found no capacity events or nodes reporting OOM.
- 2026-01-26 02:37 UTC: Noticed gaps in kv_cache.* metrics ingestion; last_observed timestamp for 2 of 6 shards is null for ~3m.
- 2026-01-26 02:45 UTC: Alert noise subsided as metric stream resumed; root cause appears to be transient telemetry export backpressure from a sidecar update.
- 2026-01-26 04:00 UTC: Postmortem notes and temporary suppressions placed.

What we observed (evidence):
- Prometheus queries showed step-like jumps in P99 derived calculation when kv_cache_hit_rate metric was missing (query fallback computed lower effective cache hits -> higher effective backend latency estimate). The alert rule did not guard against metric gaps.
- The telemetry sidecar (version 1.8.2) logged repeated 5xxs towards the aggregator between 02:10-02:26 UTC; logs correlated with a rolling deployment that morning.
- PagerDuty incident had 12 pages in 20 minutes; most were duplicates caused by a combination of alert rule sensitivity and alert grouping config that split by shard id.
- No customer-facing errors reported in Sentry or Customer Success as of 02:50 UTC.

Immediate mitigations we took: (playbook-ish)
1) Quiet/ack duplicates: used PD auto-ack for alerts that had identical fingerprint and were triggered within 2m of a higher-sev fire. (Owner: Lena)
2) Re-routed alert grouping: temporarily group by service instead of shard id to reduce duplicate pages. (Owner: Ava)
3) Suppressed the P99 SLO alert for 10m with reason "probable telemetry gap; investigating" to avoid unnecessary escalations while preserving incident timeline. (Owner: Operations)
4) Rolled back telemetry sidecar to 1.7.9 in the affected zone; metric flow restored within ~5m. (Owner: Infra)

Root cause hypothesis and why the alert fired: 
- Primary: transient failure in telemetry export (sidecar 1.8.2) caused KV cache shard metrics to be missing for a window. The SLO-derived alerting rule implicitly relies on these metrics to compute effective latency; when missing, the calculation uses a fallback path that biased the P99 estimate upward.
- Secondary: alert rule thresholds and evaluation window are too brittle to short-metric gaps; grouping by shard created duplicate pages.

Key failures in our observability design that made this noisy:
- Alerts assume presence of a metric: we treat missing metrics as trustworthy zero or fallback, which leads to false positives.
- Too fine-grained grouping: PD dedup done per shard tag -> explosion of duplicate pages.
- No pre-check in rules for metric staleness (e.g., check last_observed > now() - 2m).
- Alert severity is based purely on SLO delta over 5m; no suppression for short lived telemetry gaps.

Concrete tuning proposals (short-term):
- Change SLO alert rule to include a metric-staleness guard. Example PromQL snippet to add as a precondition: 
  up_kv_cache_last_observed_seconds > bool time() - 120
  (or use absent_over_time to prevent firing if metric missing for > 2m)
- Switch grouping/routing for SLO alerts to group by service and environment only, not shard_id. PD routing to remain one page per service.
- Increase evaluation window for SLO P99 alert from 5m to 10m with a 2m grace: this avoids reacting to micro-gaps.
- Add a secondary detection rule that tracks metric ingestion health (telemetry-export-errors > threshold) and surfaces that as an operational alert with lower page priority, not an SLO alert.

Concrete tuning proposals (longer-term / infra):
- Telemetry pipeline: add backpressure metrics, per-sidecar circuit breaker alerts, and a canary rollout gating check for sidecar version bumps.
- Runbook addition: add an explicit step when SLO alert fires to check metric staleness and telemetry exporter logs before full escalation.
- Instrument fallback behavior in SLO calculation: when key upstream metrics are absent, surface a warning state in the dashboard rather than driving the SLO metric aggressively.
- Implement a dedupe layer in the alerting stack that recognizes correlated signals (e.g., missing metric + SLO bump) and folds them into a single logical incident.

Draft runbook snippet to add (for P99 SLO burn alerts):
- Step 0 (auto): On alert trigger, check "metric-staleness" panel (Grafana) and the telemetry-exporter health query. If staleness > 2m, mark as telemetry gap and follow telemetry-gap subrunbook.
- Step 1 (human): Confirm service capacity and infra metrics (cpu, gpu_util, ecs_task_count). If capacity looks normal, deprioritize escalation.
- Step 2: Check sidecar logs for repeated 5xx or connection errors to aggregator; if present, consider rollback or restart of sidecar.
- Step 3: If metric ingestion is healthy and SLO still violated for >10m, trigger full incident and page primary SRE + product owner.

Example queries used during triage (placeholders — validate before copy/paste):
- Check metric staleness (PromQL): 
  max_over_time(kv_cache_last_observed_seconds[5m]) < time() - 120
- P99 computation fragility: show both the derived P99 and the raw request-duration histogram to confirm whether the derived value moved because of cache metrics missing.
- Telemetry exporter error rate: 
  sum(rate(telemetry_sidecar_export_errors_total[1m])) by (zone, version)

Open action items (owners & rough ETA):
- SRE-789: Add metric-staleness guard to hosted-api SLO rules and increase eval window to 10m (Owner: Diego, ETA: 2026-02-20).
- Telemetry-214: Revert or gate sidecar 1.8.x rollout and add canary gating (Owner: Priya, ETA: 2026-03-01).
- Runbook-PR: Add the above runbook steps to the SLO burn playbook and add examples of staleness checks (Owner: Lena, ETA: 2026-02-25).
- PD-routing: update alert grouping config to service-level (Owner: Ava, ETA: 2026-02-18).

Notes to self / loose observations:
- We have a class of alerts where the instrumentation is an input to a derived SLO metric. When that instrumentation is flaky, the derived metric becomes unreliable. We should avoid treating derived SLOs as raw ground truth unless we have robust input monitoring.
- Customer impact was low in this incident, but noise cost ~30m of oncall time across two engineers; measurable human cost justifies immediate small changes.
- Need to check whether any other services compute SLOs the same way (search/embeddings/deduper). Potentially broader impact.

Acceptance criteria for the short-term changes:
- No duplicate PD pages for the same service during an identical telemetry gap (test by simulating a metric gap in staging).
- SLO P99 alert does not fire for brief (<3m) metric ingestion gaps in staging or canary.
- Telemetry exporter error alert exists and is P3 (ops) to bring visibility without spamming SREs.

Follow-ups / Postmortem plan:
- Draft post-incident writeup (include evidence and timeline), attach logs & graphs, circulate to infra, serving-runtime, and product-hosted-api. (Owner: Lena)
- Convene a 30m sync with telemetry owners + SRE + serving-runtime to align on rollout gating for sidecar changes. (Owner: Priya)

Appendix: useful links captured during triage
- Grafana dashboard: Hosted API SLO overview (copy link)
- PD incident: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-9981
- Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C02SREABC/p16234

-- end of notes --

- 2026-01-27 added short-term tuning proposals after review with infra
